title: Why age is an advantage in online marketing: reframe limiting beliefs into positioning
summary: Iman argues that being young is not a handicap when selling online marketing, because business owners want someone who grew up with the platforms. He gives a general rule: objectively test each limiting belief, and if it is a real disadvantage, spin it into a selling point (age, no degree, cheap cost of living).

principles.text: Objectively test a limiting belief; if it is a real disadvantage, spin it into an advantage.
principles.quote: no matter what you believe your limiting belief is objectively assess whether it is a disadvantage and most the time it's not and if it is a disadvantage just find a way to spin it

principles.text: Clients look for the generation that grew up with the skill, so young marketers are seen as the experts.
principles.quote: when they look at you they actually see that as an advantage not a disadvantage

principles.text: Practice what you preach: being on the platforms you pitch daily is a compelling sales argument.
principles.quote: I practice what I preach you know or eat eat your own cooking right

principles.text: No degree is easy to counter because marketing knowledge goes obsolete fast; daily learning beats a credential.
principles.quote: because I don't have any certifications in digital marketing or you know I don't have a marketing degree I'm learning every single day

principles.text: Pick fields where results beat track record: online marketing is early, so businesses are only now hunting for help.
principles.quote: online marketing at the moment is kind of like this eighth wonder you know it's kind of this thing where businesses are just starting in a catch up

principles.text: Turn a geographic or cost disadvantage into an offer: more dedication and lower price because you do not pay inflated rent.
principles.quote: you're not spending the on increased expertise or increased knowledge you're just spending that on their increased rent
